backlog.title: Accelerating Manufacturing-Aware Simulations For Photonic Integrated Circuits With FTCO And Digital Twins
backlog.summary:
Fab workflow connects GDS layout import, 3D process simulation, GPU-accelerated FDTD, design of experiments, with AI-based surrogate modeling.
The post Accelerating Manufacturing-Aware Simulations For Photonic Integrated Circuits With FTCO And Digital Twins appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: New Fab Technology Co-Optimization (FTCO) workflows now integrate GDS layout data with 3D process simulation and AI-based surrogate modeling to account for real-world fabrication variations.
GPU-accelerated FDTD simulations can now process complex 3D models with 65 million cells in under 10 hours, significantly speeding up design cycles.
The use of digital twins allows non-simulation experts to intuitively understand the relationship between manufacturing process variations and final photonic circuit performance.

backlog.title: Scaling CPO Testing Beyond A Single Die
backlog.summary:
Fiber alignment, connector durability, and simultaneous optical and electrical testing pose challenges for high-volume manufacturing.
The post Scaling CPO Testing Beyond A Single Die appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: High-volume manufacturing of Co-Packaged Optics (CPO) is currently constrained by single-site testing limitations, primarily due to the complexities of fiber alignment.
While NPO (Near-Packaged Optics) and CPO architectures are evolving, the industry is actively seeking multi-site testing solutions to improve throughput and reduce costs.
Testing high-power ASICs alongside optical engines presents significant challenges in power delivery and thermal management, complicating the transition to parallel testing.

The post Scaling Data Movement For Physical AI appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Physical AI systems require a strategic balance between compute elements and data movement to maintain real-time decision-making while preserving battery life.
Engineers are increasingly differentiating between coherent interconnects for CPUs and non-coherent interconnects for AI accelerators to optimize system efficiency.
The industry is facing significant challenges in managing data streams in heterogeneous architectures, necessitating new approaches to chip design and interconnect scaling.

backlog.title: Nuclear-powered spaceships
backlog.summary: Just before the Artemis II crew began its historic slingshot around the moon this past April, NASA announced plans to build Space Reactor-1 Freedom. SR-1, the first-ever nuclear-reactor-­powered interplanetary spacecraft, is meant to fly an uncrewed mission to Mars by the end of 2028, arriving in 2029. A successful mission would herald a new era…
bullets: NASA is investing $2 billion into nuclear electric propulsion, which utilizes uranium-atom-splitting reactions to generate electricity for ion-based thrust.
The agency plans to launch the uncrewed Space Reactor-1 (SR-1) mission to Mars by late 2028, aiming to significantly reduce travel time and cosmic radiation exposure for future astronauts.

While previous programs like DRACO were canceled due to high costs and safety testing challenges, experts believe nuclear propulsion is technically viable and essential for efficient interplanetary travel.

backlog.title: Exercise in a pill
backlog.summary: We all know exercise is good for us. It builds muscle, strengthens bones, lowers blood pressure, and boosts mood. By deciphering how movement benefits the body, researchers hope to develop medicines that can offer some of the same perks—without the workout. The idea isn’t to replace exercise but to bring its upsides to people who…
bullets: Researchers are identifying molecular pathways triggered by physical activity to develop pharmaceuticals that mimic the health benefits of exercise for patients with frailty or chronic illness.
The biotech firm Pelagos is developing a compound that targets specific receptors in muscle cells to boost endurance, with early mouse studies showing improved cognitive and heart health.
Regulatory hurdles remain significant, as the FDA currently approves drugs for disease treatment rather than wellness enhancement, and over 90% of human clinical trials fail.

backlog.title: Cleaning up PFAS
backlog.summary: Scrubbing Earth of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances—a.k.a. PFAS or forever chemicals—could eliminate a list of woes for people and planet. Used for decades in everything from nonstick pans to firefighting foams, PFAS have been linked to increased risks of fertility challenges, developmental delays, cancer, and reduced immune response. They are known for a strong bond…
bullets: PFAS 'forever chemicals' are pervasive in the environment, with 89% of the US population showing blood plasma levels above common thresholds for potential health risks.
Current cleanup efforts focus on trapping chemicals via reverse osmosis or foam fractionation, though these methods leave behind contaminated brine that requires expensive destruction.
Electrochemical degradation, a method using electrodes to break down the carbon-fluorine bonds in PFAS, has demonstrated over 90% efficiency in tests and is being commercialized by AECOM.

backlog.title: Stacked-Die Multi-Chip Architectures: The Tradeoff Between Scaling And Power Delivery
backlog.summary:
Integrated voltage regulators reduce current density, provide higher regulation bandwidth, and reduce reliance on large decoupling capacitor networks. 
The post Stacked-Die Multi-Chip Architectures: The Tradeoff Between Scaling And Power Delivery appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: The shift toward stacked-die and multi-chip architectures for AI and HPC has created significant power delivery bottlenecks, including increased current density and voltage droop.
Integrated Voltage Regulators (IVRs) are being deployed closer to the load to enable higher-voltage distribution and reduce reliance on large, inefficient decoupling capacitor networks.
Designers are currently forced to use voltage guard bands to maintain reliability, which limits the performance and efficiency of high-density silicon.
Advanced packaging introduces a direct conflict between signal density and power delivery, requiring new innovations in package-integrated magnetic inductors and capacitive chiplets.

backlog.title: How Self-Aligned CFET Technology Could Extend CMOS Scaling Beyond 10 Å
backlog.summary:
A process sequence for SRAM and logic that delivers higher performance through larger effective channel width and improved electrostatics at smaller nodes.
The post How Self-Aligned CFET Technology Could Extend CMOS Scaling Beyond 10 Å appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Self-aligned Complementary Field-Effect Transistor (SA-CFET) architecture vertically stacks NMOS and PMOS devices to overcome the physical limitations of current gate-all-around nanosheets.
Digital twin modeling demonstrates that SA-CFET can achieve a 52.7% area reduction compared to N3 technology, enabling a 0.0094 μm² SRAM bit cell.
The architecture utilizes three key self-aligned modules—buried power rails, contacts, and through-silicon vias—to mitigate contact crowding and improve process margins.
This design addresses critical integration hurdles like metal gate isolation and electrical shorts, providing a viable path for scaling beyond the 10 angstrom node.

backlog.title: Beyond The EPE Budget: Building The Next Generation Of Computational Lithography
backlog.summary:
Why better models, richer metrology, explainable AI, and cross-industry collaboration must come together to extend semiconductor scaling.
The post Beyond The EPE Budget: Building The Next Generation Of Computational Lithography appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Edge Placement Error (EPE) has evolved from a narrow lithography metric into a critical system-level indicator of manufacturing yield and design intent.
Industry experts identify Optical Proximity Correction (OPC) as both a primary source of EPE and the most promising avenue for future error reduction.
Scaling challenges are increasingly driven by an unbounded EPE budget, encompassing variables from mask 3D effects and resist variability to etch and downstream integration.
The industry is shifting away from empirical rule-based corrections toward more sophisticated, explainable AI models to manage complex process interactions.

backlog.title: Self-Heating And Parasitics Challenge Multi-Tier CFET Scaling (TU Munich, IIT Kanpur)
backlog.summary:
Researchers at the Technical University of Munich and Indian Institute of Technology Kanpur published “Self-Heating and Parasitic Effects in Multi-Tier CFET Design.” Abstract Excerpt: “We study the impact of self-heating effects (SHEs) and middle of line (MOL) and back-end of line (BEOL) induced parasitics on multi-tier CFET design, where multiple nanosheet devices are vertically stacked.... » read more
The post Self-Heating And Parasitics Challenge Multi-Tier CFET Scaling (TU Munich, IIT Kanpur) appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Researchers from TU Munich and IIT Kanpur analyzed the impact of self-heating effects and parasitic RC networks on multi-tier Complementary FET (CFET) designs.
The study compared four-tier CFET architectures against conventional two-tier designs using TCAD models calibrated to experimental data to map temperature profiles.

Findings indicate that as nanosheet devices are vertically stacked, thermal management and interconnect parasitics become significant bottlenecks for scaling, requiring careful design optimization in the middle and back-end of line.

bullets: Testing costs for optical components currently rival manufacturing costs, necessitating new strategies for failure diagnosis and cost control in advanced packages.
Engineers are increasingly incorporating monitor photodiodes and loopback capabilities into optical engines to facilitate better failure analysis and mission-mode testing.

Accurate de-embedding of optical and electrical boundaries is essential for identifying failure origins, requiring the use of golden reference sources and standardized measurement planes across test insertions.

Foundries are increasingly moving into the backend space, while OSATs are adopting lithography-related materials and processes historically reserved for wafer fabs.
This convergence is driven by the complexity of advanced packaging, which requires tighter integration between front-end fabrication and final assembly.
Industry leaders emphasize the need for shared, physics-grounded design tools that connect silos across equipment, fabrication, and packaging to improve manufacturing flexibility.

backlog.title: What Breaks When Packaging Moves From Wafer To Panel?
backlog.summary:
Engineers are discovering many things they thought were process assumptions were actually wafer assumptions.
The post What Breaks When Packaging Moves From Wafer To Panel? appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Transitioning from 300mm wafers to 600mm panels offers significant economic advantages by reducing edge waste and increasing the number of units per process cycle.
The industry faces a major hurdle because existing equipment, materials, and process controls were engineered specifically for the geometry and mechanical behavior of round wafers.
To mitigate risk, some manufacturers are adopting a hybrid approach: processing large-format interposers on panels before dividing them into smaller pieces for assembly.
The move to panel-level packaging is revealing that many long-standing process assumptions were actually implicit dependencies on wafer dimensions.

backlog.title: PVTW: Extending Silicon Characterization From PVT To Real-World Workload
backlog.summary:
Two devices operating at exactly the same voltage, frequency, and temperature can behave differently depending on what they are being asked to do.
The post PVTW: Extending Silicon Characterization From PVT To Real-World Workload appeared first on Semiconductor Engineering.
bullets: Traditional silicon characterization based on Process, Voltage, and Temperature (PVT) is insufficient for modern high-performance AI processors.
The proposed PVTW methodology adds 'Workload' as a fourth dimension to account for how specific software tasks impact silicon behavior and power consumption.
A hybrid architecture combining Automated Test Equipment (ATE) for electrical precision and System Level Test (SLT) for realistic application environments is recommended for comprehensive validation.
This approach allows manufacturers to maintain electrical control while exercising specific architectural components like SRAM, SerDes, and compute engines under real-world stress.

backlog.title: Interspecies communication
backlog.summary: Humans are far from the only species with a gift for gab, and our furry, feathered, and finned friends could have a lot to tell us. Decoding how animals communicate with one another could offer a window into the inner lives of other species and help humans realize that “animals are sentient creatures who think,…
bullets: The Earth Species Project (ESP) is utilizing machine learning and large language models to analyze animal vocalizations and identify patterns in interspecies communication.
Researchers are training 'NatureLM' on a dataset of human speech, music, and animal sounds to attempt the translation of vocalizations from species like carrion crows.

The field faces significant challenges, including the difficulty of interpreting non-auditory signals like pheromones and the lack of a 'Rosetta stone' to verify the accuracy of AI-generated translations.

backlog.title: Eliminating traffic deaths
backlog.summary: Every year, traffic crashes kill more than one million people, and they’re the leading cause of death for children and young adults. In the US, 100 people a day lose their lives this way, in many cases not on highways but on rural and local streets. “Traffic deaths are a leading cause of preventable death,…
bullets: Traffic crashes kill over one million people annually, making them a leading cause of preventable death for children and young adults globally.

Cities like Hoboken, New Jersey, have achieved zero traffic fatalities since 2017 by implementing infrastructure changes such as curb extensions, improved public transit, and data-driven intersection redesigns.
Widespread adoption of safety measures is often hindered by government bureaucracy and the difficulty of justifying the removal of parking or road space for pedestrian-focused infrastructure.

backlog.title: Three things you should know about permafrost
backlog.summary: How much do you know about permafrost? Maybe, like me, you’ve been aware that this layer of frozen soil is thawing, that it’s important in the global puzzle of climate change … and that’s about the extent of it.   The great news for both of us is that my colleague James Temple just published two…
bullets: Arctic permafrost has shrunk by approximately 12% since 1850, with the rate of loss accelerating significantly over the last 50 years.
Current UN climate models largely fail to account for the abrupt thaw and collapse of permafrost, suggesting that global warming projections may be underestimated.
The thawing of permafrost creates a dangerous feedback loop where microbes release trapped greenhouse gases, further accelerating global temperature increases.

backlog.title: Industrial Intelligence: The next growth opportunity for manufacturing
backlog.summary: Every manufacturer has its own industrial intelligence. Some is documented, and some resides in the knowledge of experienced workers. Consider an experienced operator preparing to restart a line after a changeover. The machine settings matter, but so does knowing how a particular material behaves, what happened during the previous shift, and when an apparently minor…
bullets: Manufacturers are increasingly focusing on 'Industrial Intelligence,' which seeks to digitize and scale the tacit knowledge and judgment of experienced workers across entire organizations.
The integration of Physical AI allows systems to perceive, reason, and act within manufacturing environments, moving beyond simple data collection to automated decision-making.
By connecting fragmented operational data with human expertise, companies aim to improve process efficiency and innovation, turning localized know-how into a scalable competitive advantage.

backlog.title: How solid-state transformers could help power the AI boom
backlog.summary: Transformers are a crucial but nearly invisible part of our grid. The devices help efficiently move power across long distances, but they’re complicated and in short supply. And given that their basic design hasn’t changed much for about a century, they could use an upgrade.  As the world races to meet rising electricity demand from…
bullets: Solid-state transformers are being developed to modernize the aging electrical grid, which currently relies on century-old designs that are struggling to meet demand from data centers and EVs.
Unlike traditional transformers that use heavy copper and steel, solid-state versions utilize high-power semiconductors to offer greater control over electricity flow and improved efficiency.

While currently limited in their ability to handle the highest voltages for long-distance transmission, these devices represent a critical path toward reducing energy loss and alleviating supply chain bottlenecks in power infrastructure.
